newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya shilling rallies on dlr, demand subdued.
newsitem.headline: Kenya shilling rallies on dlr, demand subdued.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling continued to rally against the dollar on the back of inflows from the tea sector and amid subdued demand, commercial dealers said.
They said there was strong interbank activity, with banks buying dollars, but the only exceptional factor in the market was that the Central Bank of Kenya was not buying dollars.
"The central bank normally buys a lot of the excess dollars from the market but they have not done that the entire past week," a senior commercial dealer said. "That's exceptional."
A leading dealer said the shilling was "appreciating like mad", amid a good supply of dollars and minimal demand.
The dealer said tea inflows mainly were responsible for the dollars but a few non-governmental organisations (NGOs) were also active. He also noted demand was very subdued.
The central bank posted a commercial mean of 53.96 versus the dollar compared with 54 on Thursday. The bank posted the pound at a mean rate of 88.155, compared with 87.75 on Thursday.

"There is a lot of selling in the interbank, which brought the shilling rate to around 53.60/90 versus the dollar in the morning, and strengthening further to the 53.10/50 range in early afternoon," one trader said.
"Some of the money (dollars) was carried forward from yesterday (Thursday). The central bank is also not buying and not supporting the shilling at the current level," he added.
Liquidity in the money market was tight, with overnight rates firmly in the lower teens. That meant rates were virtually unchanged from the 12 percent range of Thursday.
